sections.title: The group -gh(t)
paragraphs: The letter group -gh(t) makes no sound at all. In the word (night) /naɪt/, which means night, the middle letters stay silent. You hear only the surrounding sounds. This group has one single spoken pattern.

sections.title: How to say -gh(t)
paragraphs: Do not move your tongue or lips for these letters. Let the air pass straight to the final sound without pausing. You make no voice and no friction in your throat. Your vocal cords do not vibrate until the next letter.

sections.title: Spelling of -gh(t)
paragraphs: Before the letter t, the group gh is always completely silent. You see this pattern in common words like (light) /laɪt/ and (sight) /saɪt/. Just jump over the two middle letters when you read.

sections.title: Comparing -gh(t)
paragraphs: Learners often try to pronounce a rough scraping sound in their throat. Do not make any sound like the end of the Scottish word loch. Keep your throat open and silent, moving straight to the next spoken sound.
